description: Golden questions grounded in the six public external policy PDFs. Institutions remain source-scoped.

cases.question: Which institution publishes the Employee Handbook?
cases.expected_answer: The University of Southern Mississippi publishes it through University Human Resources.

evidence.fact: The opening identifies University Human Resources and the University of Southern Mississippi.

cases.question: What edition does the University of Southern Mississippi employee handbook identify itself as?
cases.expected_answer: The May 2026 edition.

evidence.fact: The edition text states May 2026.

cases.question: Is the University of Southern Mississippi handbook a contract?
cases.expected_answer: No. It states that the handbook is not a contract and does not create contractual rights.

evidence.fact: About This Handbook says it is not a contract and policies do not give rise to contractual rights.

cases.question: Who may change, eliminate, or supplement the University of Southern Mississippi handbook policies?
cases.expected_answer: The University reserves the right to make those changes as needed, with or without notice to employees.

evidence.fact: The handbook says the University reserves the right to change, eliminate, and supplement policies.

cases.question: What topics are covered by the University of Southern Mississippi handbook?
cases.expected_answer: It includes employment conditions, performance, termination, benefits, records, and other staff policies.

evidence.fact: The documented structure includes definitions, employment conditions, performance, termination, benefits, and records.

cases.question: Which institution issued the remote work policy?
cases.expected_answer: Yeshiva University issued the remote work policy.

evidence.fact: The inventory and document identify Yeshiva University.

cases.question: What is the title shown for the Yeshiva document?
cases.expected_answer: REMOTE WORK POLICY.

evidence.fact: The first page contains REMOTE WORK POLICY.

cases.question: Does the Yeshiva document cover remote work elements?
cases.expected_answer: Yes. It includes a section titled REMOTE WORK ELEMENTS.

evidence.fact: The document includes REMOTE WORK ELEMENTS.

cases.question: How many pages does the Yeshiva remote work policy contain?
cases.expected_answer: Nine pages.

evidence.fact: The inspected PDF has 9 pages.

cases.question: Who is listed as the author in the Yeshiva PDF metadata?
cases.expected_answer: Julie Auster.

evidence.fact: PDF metadata identifies Julie Auster as author.

cases.question: Which organization issued the acceptable-use policy?
cases.expected_answer: King's College London.

evidence.fact: The document identifies King's College London.

cases.question: What version and effective date are recorded for the King's acceptable-use policy?
cases.expected_answer: Version V10.8, effective June 4, 2026.

evidence.fact: The policy records version V10.8 and effective date June 4, 2026.

cases.question: When was the King's acceptable-use policy last reviewed?

evidence.fact: Last reviewed May 19, 2026.

cases.question: What broad areas does the King's acceptable-use policy cover?
cases.expected_answer: Credentials, access, remote work, security, equipment, personal use, email, monitoring, and reporting.

evidence.fact: The structure lists credentials, access, remote work, security, equipment, personal use, email, monitoring, and reporting.

cases.question: What is the next review date recorded for the King's acceptable-use policy?

evidence.fact: The next review is recorded as May 19, 2027.

cases.question: Which organization is identified by the BYOD procedure?
cases.expected_answer: King's College London, identified in the procedure as King's IT.

evidence.fact: The document identifies King's IT and King's College London provenance.

cases.question: What version is recorded for the BYOD procedure?
cases.expected_answer: Version 3.0.

evidence.fact: The procedure records version 3.0.

cases.question: What is the effective date of the BYOD procedure?
cases.expected_answer: November 1, 2021.

evidence.fact: The effective date is November 1, 2021.

cases.question: What areas does the BYOD procedure address?
cases.expected_answer: Personal-device security, maintenance, data governance, loss or unauthorized access, responsibilities, and annual review.

evidence.fact: The structure includes responsibilities, personal-device security, maintenance, data governance, loss or unauthorized access, and annual review.

cases.question: When was the BYOD procedure last reviewed?
cases.expected_answer: August 28, 2025.

evidence.fact: Last reviewed August 28, 2025.

cases.question: Which institution issued the Employee Travel and Expense Policy?
cases.expected_answer: Suffolk University Finance & Accounting issued it.

evidence.fact: The policy is approved and distributed by Suffolk University Finance & Accounting.

cases.question: To whom does the Suffolk travel and expense policy apply?
cases.expected_answer: Any employee who incurs business and travel-related expenses paid by Suffolk University.

evidence.fact: The policy states that it applies to any employee incurring business and travel-related expenses paid by Suffolk.

cases.question: What is the latest revision date recorded for the Suffolk policy?
cases.expected_answer: December 1, 2021.

evidence.fact: The policy metadata records latest revision date December 1, 2021.

cases.question: Which institution issued the Travel and Expense Reimbursement Procedures effective July 1, 2022?
cases.expected_answer: Temple University, through the Office of the President and finance officers.

evidence.fact: The title page identifies Temple University and the Office of the President.

cases.question: What standard does Temple state for reimbursable travel expenses?
cases.expected_answer: Travelers should incur the lowest reasonable travel expenses, and reimbursement is for reasonable and necessary approved work-related travel expenses.

evidence.fact: The purpose and scope states reasonable and necessary expenses, lowest reasonable travel expenses, and approved work-related travel.

cases.question: How must most Temple travel arrangements be made?
cases.expected_answer: Through Concur or World Travel, except for the stated conference-related exception and approved service exceptions.

evidence.fact: Booking generally requires Concur or World Travel, with exceptions when those services cannot provide service.

cases.question: Which Temple procedure topics include meals, receipts, and submission due dates?
cases.expected_answer: The procedures have sections for meals, receipts, and submission due dates.

evidence.fact: The contents list Meals, Receipts, and Submission Due Dates.

cases.question: Which two documents are King's College London IT documents, and how do their scopes differ?
cases.expected_answer: The acceptable-use policy is the broader governing policy; the BYOD procedure specializes in unmanaged personal devices.

evidence.fact: The inspection report distinguishes the broader acceptable-use policy from the BYOD procedure.

cases.question: Which two finance documents come from different universities?
cases.expected_answer: Suffolk University provides the Employee Travel and Expense Policy, while Temple University provides the Travel and Expense Reimbursement Procedures.

evidence.fact: The inventory identifies Suffolk and Temple as separate source organizations.

cases.question: Why should the Suffolk and Temple travel rules not be merged into one policy?
cases.expected_answer: Their approval chains, rates, exceptions, lodging and meal rules, and effective dates belong to different universities.

evidence.fact: The inspection report explicitly warns that the policies are source-scoped and must not be merged.

cases.question: How do the USM handbook and Yeshiva remote-work policy differ in scope?
cases.expected_answer: The USM handbook is broad HR guidance, while the Yeshiva document is a focused remote-work policy.

evidence.fact: The inspection report distinguishes broad handbook guidance from focused remote-work material.

cases.question: Which source has the later stated effective date: the King's acceptable-use policy or the BYOD procedure?
cases.expected_answer: The acceptable-use policy, effective June 4, 2026, is later than the BYOD procedure, effective November 1, 2021.

evidence.fact: The two documents record effective dates June 4, 2026 and November 1, 2021.

cases.question: What is the company's universal per-diem limit across all six documents?
cases.expected_answer: The corpus does not define one universal company-wide per-diem limit; the documents belong to different institutions.

evidence.fact: The inspection report warns that policies from different institutions must not be merged.

cases.question: What is the employee's personal salary in the dataset?
cases.expected_answer: The corpus contains no employee personal salary information.

cases.question: Which policy applies to our company's 2026 expense approval workflow?
cases.expected_answer: The corpus does not contain a policy for an unspecified company; it contains public references from named universities.

cases.question: What is the current employee's home address?
cases.expected_answer: The corpus contains no employee home addresses or other personal contact records.

cases.question: What is the single mandatory BYOD rule for every employer?
cases.expected_answer: No universal rule can be derived because the BYOD procedure is a King's College London source document and does not govern every employer.
